Citing the use of AI-generated/assisted work (e.g., using GitHub
Copilot for project work):

If the use of the tool was localized to a few places (e.g., used it to
write a few methods/classes only), cite its use in comments near where
you used it.

If the use was more widespread (e.g., used AI to generate most of your
code), cite the usage (i.e., which tool, who used it, the extent of
use) in the following location instead (i.e., no need to cite in code
comments):
    iP: in the README file
    tP: in the DG, under the Acknowledgements section

Use of AI

This course aims to get you started on AI-assisted SE in a way that does
not compromise (and possibly enhances) your learning of basic SE skills.

A non-trivial amount of AI use is expected. Aim to use AI at least 20%
of the time when doing course-related work, on average.

The level of AI use in coding tasks can vary as follows -- based on how
much manual work happens and at which point.

    AI-1
    No AI use. Hand-code everything. Use AI as a 'smart search engine'
    to ask general questions.
    Use this level when doing SE tasks that are very new to you.
    AI-2
    Hand-code first, with AI's feedback: You hand-code the first version
    as if there is no AI. Ask AI to review. Refine based on AI's
    feedback.
    Operating at this level (on avearge) is enough to meet the minimum
    requirement of AI use the course expects.
    AI-3
    Hand-code to start, get AI to finish: You hand-code a minimal
    version, just a proof-of-concept. Get AI to strengthen it to a
    full-fledged version e.g., handle edge cases, add tests.
    AI-4
    'Think' and compare: Think of how you would do the task manually.
    Get AI to do it. Compare the solution you 'imagined' with the one
    AI produced.
    AI-5
    AI codes, you review: Get AI to do the task. Review it yourself
    fully, including the code, tests, behavior etc.
    AI-6
    Full AI: Get AI to do the task, fully, including the review. Only
    review the outcome (e.g., the feature behavior).
    Use this level sparingly, if at all. As you will be graded for code
    quality, it is not prudent not to review the AI-generated code at
    all.

Which level to use? Depends on the task, how well can do the task
manually, and your learning goals.

    Hand-coding will teach you basic SE skills. Using AI more will save
    time and also teach you how to use AI for SE.
    Recommended: First learn to do the task manually (i.e., Levels AI-1,
    AI-2).
    As you become more confident of your ability to do that task
    manually, move to higher levels of AI use (i.e., AI-3 and higher)
    to do the same task faster.
    If you can't explain what AI did, your level of AI use is too high.

commitResults.messageBody:
viewappt answers "who has an appointment when?" for every patient at
once, so a nurse who asks "when is Alex seen next?" has to spot Alex
in the list and read the page day by day. A plain viewappt, meanwhile,
is rejected as a format error, although "the upcoming appointments"
is the question the command answers most naturally.

Let's give viewappt an optional --id ID, and make a plain viewappt
show the appointments from today onwards:

* --id combines with a DATE, --from and --to in any order. It narrows
  both the appointment page and the patient list to that patient; an
  unknown ID fails, and leaves the view and the list as they were.
* The result carries the ID in AppointmentRange, so the appointment
  view filters its page to that patient, and Esc shows everyone again.
* The message counts that patient's appointments in the range, so a
  patient seen twice on the day reads "2 appointment(s)", while the
  all-patients messages keep counting patients.
* An ID keeps to one token, so a date typed after the options is
  rejected instead of being swallowed into the ID.

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat a non-breaking space as an option separator
commitResults.messageBody:
A non-breaking space copies in invisibly from formatted text, and
the argument tokenizer cannot distinguish it from a space once the
user sees their input. Because Java's \s does not match U+00A0,
and trim does not strip it either, an option typed beside one was
glued either to the previous word or to its own value, so a
correctly typed --name was rejected with the generic unsupported
option error. Copying variability is a known reality for people
pasting commands from written handovers, not a malformed command.

Key changes:
- Translate U+00A0 to a plain space at the entry of
  ArgumentTokenizer.normalizeOptionSeparators, where all the
  option-aware parsing flows through
- Add a tokenizer test pinning that NBSP separators produce the
  same output as typed spaces and unknown options still fail
- Add an add-parser test running a full valid command whose
  separators beside --name and --phone are NBSPs
- Note the non-breaking space behaviour in the separator rules
  of the add, edit and find sections of the UG

the four-digit pad, so a value such as +12345-01-01 was parsed as
a fully real appointment day that no human meant to book.

Key changes:
- Guard the parsed shape at exactly four unsigned digits
  \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} before LocalDate.parse
- Keep year 0000 accepted, as ISO-8601 represents it, so this is
  a shape guard rather than a range rule
- Add the first parseDate tests: a valid date, year 0000,
  non-existent 2026-02-30, and signed or wider years
- State the four-digit unsigned-year rule in the UG date rule
  and in the DG date-error paragraph under viewappt

commitResults.messageTitle: Move appointment searches from find to viewappt

appointment only, through Patient#getNextAppointment(). Since #90 lets
a patient have several appointments, find misses appointments that
viewappt finds. Substring matching is also ambiguous for dates: "10"
matches October, the 10th of any month and 10:00.

and viewappt handles every appointment search with real dates.

* remove the appointment option from find, and delete
  Patient#getNextAppointment() and PatientBuilder#withNextAppointment

  --from the range starts today, and without --till it has no end. A
  --till date before today with no --from is an error, as the range
  would be empty
* rename add's --next-appointment to --appt, since it adds any number
  of past or future appointments and edit already uses --add-appt

compares dates only, so a visit earlier today still shows up.

commitResults.messageBody:

typed out in full, in lowercase.

of the v1.5 GUI vote in #163):

  passes the patient ID that a command takes first to IdCompleter.
  Each Completion carries the word it fills in, for the hint.
* Words match ignoring case, but command words, options and help
  topics are filled in lowercase, the only case the parsers accept.
* CommandBox updates the completions as the text changes, and after
  the only match it moves on, so addap gives addappt, then an ID.
* StatusBarFooter shows a Tab key cap and at most five matches, then
  how many more. The save location moves to the right end, where it
  stays, so that it does not jump while the user types.

result of the last command. The team chose this design in the vote.

commitResults.messageBody:
The data file saves an appointment's mark as "done". The nurse decides
what a mark means, and the GUI now shows it as a pin, so "done" claims
too much in the file as well (#211).

Let's save it as "marked". A file from v1.5 or earlier that saved
"done" still loads, and "marked" wins if a file has both.

commitResults.messageTitle: Word clash warnings for the patient's own visits
commitResults.messageBody:
A clash warning names every clashing appointment with its patient, so
a visit that clashes with another visit of the same patient repeats the
patient that the result already names, as in "Added appointment 2 of
ALEX YEOH (S1234567A) ... it clashes with ALEX YEOH (S1234567A),
appointment #1."

Let's name such a visit "this patient's appointment #1", and keep the
name and ID for another patient's.

The usage of markappt also does not say that a done appointment no
longer clashes, and the UG does not say that marking one of two
clashing visits removes the clash from both. Let's say so.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move the time closer to the date in the details
commitResults.messageBody:
In the details, the time sits after a 150-pixel date column, so it is
far from a short date such as "Mon 23 Nov", now that the number has
its own column before the date.

Let's narrow the date column to 130 pixels, which still fits a date
with a year, and widen the time column by the same 20 pixels, so that
the time moves left and the details stay where they are.

commitResults.messageTitle: Line up the list counts across both lists
commitResults.messageBody:
Each list header ends where its rows end, which is one scroll bar
further in while the list shows a scroll bar. The week view usually
has one and the patient list often does not, so "6 patients" and
"7 appointments" end in different places as the user switches views.

Let's always end the headers one scroll bar in, and have the cells of
a list without a scroll bar leave its width empty at their end. The
rows and the counts of both lists then end in the same place, with or
without a scroll bar.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show clashing next appointments in red
commitResults.messageBody:
A clash is red in the appointment list and in the details, but a
patient's next appointment in the patient list shows no clash, so a
nurse who stays on the patient list does not see it (#211).

Let's color a patient's next appointment red when it clashes, also
when it is today, so red wins over today's orange. The patient list
now takes the list of all appointments, and refreshes its rows when
any appointment changes, since a change to one patient can make
another patient's appointment clash.

commitResults.messageBody:
The pin takes the same 16-pixel square as the clash mark, but tilted

middle, so it looks smaller than the clash mark's box beside it.

Let's enlarge it to about 14 pixels and center it. Let's also add

the style sheet's color, for settings that may change what a mark
means (#216).

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix add command option parsing and documentation
commitResults.messageBody:
Empty trailing optional flags and unknown options can become patient
details. Tab separators prevent valid options from being recognized,
and the user guide describes the old add syntax.

These gaps can save unintended patient data and reject valid input.
Outdated examples also make the supported command harder to use.

Reject unknown options and unsupported --name=value syntax with usage
instructions. Report empty trailing values through the existing field
validators, and retain unordered parameters and both optional fields.
Update the user guide with the supported syntax and field rules.

Keeping changes inside the add parser preserves shared behavior and
reduces overlap with teammates' work. The existing command, tokenizer,
validators, and field rules remain in use.

Add 19 regression and integration tests for reordered options, optional
fields, invalid input, JSON persistence, and unchanged model and file
state after rejection.

Checkstyle checks. git diff --check also passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add substring filters to the find command
commitResults.messageBody:
The find command searches whole words in patient names and accepts
bare keywords. It cannot search other patient fields or partial values.

Nurses need to locate patients using incomplete details such as an
ID fragment, an address phrase, or part of a medical history.

Replace bare keywords with optional filters for ID, name, address,
phone number, medical history, and next appointment. Require at least
one non-blank value and match any supplied field using a contiguous
substring. Ignore case and repeated whitespace, and accept optional
straight or curly double quotes around complete values.

Reject duplicate and unknown options, unexpected preamble text,
malformed quotes, and --option=value syntax. Preserve the displayed
list when parsing fails. Search all patients on each valid command,
preserving their order and returning each matching patient once.

Use OR matching so that any supplied detail can identify a patient.
Reuse existing parsing, normalization, and filtering utilities to
follow project conventions and minimize changes to shared code.

Update the User Guide and Developer Guide with the command format,
examples, implementation notes, use case, and manual test scenarios.
Add tests for all fields, quotation handling, invalid input, OR
matching, successive searches, and restoring the complete list.

Validation: the full test suite, checkstyleMain, checkstyleTest, and
git diff --check pass.
Add QoL improvements

commitResults.messageTitle: Rank find results by number of matching fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Find returns patients in stored list order even when they match
different numbers of supplied search fields.

Patients matching more fields are more relevant to a search with
several criteria and should appear before less relevant matches.

Rank results by descending number of matching fields. Count each
supplied field once and retain the stored list order for ties.

Reuse the existing matching rules to keep filtering and ranking
consistent. Keep sorting confined to the displayed results so that
stored patient order and appointment lists remain unchanged.
Restore normal ordering when list, add, edit or viewappt replaces
the search filter.

Add assertions, null checks, logging and regression tests for match
counts, ties, live updates and ordering resets. Update command help,
the User Guide and the Developer Guide to explain the behavior.

Validation: ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon check coverage passes
with 578 tests, no failures and clean Checkstyle results.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable patient notes in existing commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Patients can store notes and display them in the detail panel, but
commands cannot add, edit or search them.

Nurses need to record personal information outside the other patient
fields, such as hobbies, pet peeves and daily routines, to better
understand their patients.

Add optional --notes support to add, edit and find, and include notes
in patient feedback. Preserve existing notes when edits omit the
option, and reject blank or repeated notes options. Retain uppercase
normalisation and case-insensitive substring searches with OR matching.

Reuse the existing notes model, storage, detail panel and shared
option parser to maintain consistency and limit changes to shared
code. Continue displaying notes through view without adding commands.

Update command help and the User and Developer Guides. Add assertions,
validation, logging and regression tests covering notes, persistence,
invalid input and preservation during unrelated edits.

Validation: All 581 tests pass, along with Checkstyle, coverage and
repository checks. JavaFX smoke tests confirm live updates and notes
display after restarting with saved data.
Update uml diagrams

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a sequence diagram for 'find' command
Number appointments and warn about clashes
commitResults.messageBody:
Appointments use date and time as identity, and a patient's schedule
keeps only one visit at each timestamp. Adding or moving another visit
to that time is rejected, while loading duplicate times can discard
visits. Clashes between different patients have no warning.

Nurses may intentionally plan visits at the same time. They need to
keep every visit and identify it reliably after its date or time changes.

Assign each appointment an immutable number within its patient. Use
the highest remaining number plus one for new visits, preserve numbers
during edits, and leave surviving numbers unchanged after deletion.

Support numbers in editappt and deleteappt while retaining --appt
selectors. Reject ambiguous timestamp selectors with numbered matches.
Persist numbers and assign missing legacy numbers chronologically,
preserving every same-time visit and its details. Reject invalid or
duplicate explicit numbers without silently dropping appointments.

Allow clashes and append warnings naming the conflicting patients and
appointment numbers. Show stable numbers in the appointment list and
patient details. Mark clashing dates, times and day headings in red,
preserving clash colors for past and selected visits.

Detect clashes against all appointments, including hidden patients,
and refresh highlighting when appointments change. Reuse shared lookup,
parser, model and JavaFX components to keep behavior consistent across
commands and views.

Add assertions, validation exceptions and diagnostic logging. Update
the user and developer guides, manual testing instructions, UML sources
and rendered diagrams.

Add regression coverage for numbering, migration, selectors, warnings,
persistence and GUI rendering. All 761 tests pass, together with
Checkstyle, coverage and repository checks.

Refs #154, #155

Appointments have stable patient-local numbers but no completion status.
Date-based past and upcoming groups do not record whether a visit is
complete.

Nurses need to record completed visits without deleting appointments,
and correct mistaken completions without recreating their details.

Add markappt ID NUMBER and unmarkappt ID NUMBER to change completion
using patient IDs and stable appointment numbers. Allow appointments on
any date, including those of patients hidden by filters. Reject missing
patients, missing appointments and repeated status changes without
changing data or the view.

Add immutable completion status and persist it as a JSON boolean.
Load older appointments as undone and reject non-boolean status values.
Preserve completion during numbering, rescheduling and details edits,
while starting new appointments as undone.

Show Done and Undone labels in appointment rows and patient details.
Keep done visits visible, but exclude them from patient next-appointment
summaries and clash detection. Restore applicable warnings and red
highlighting when unmarking. Retain date-based grouping, counts, ordering
and automatic appointment-list selection.

Select the updated appointment in the Appointments view, keeping the
displayed page when it contains the visit. Register both commands in
help and patient ID Tab completion.

Reuse existing lookup, navigation and refresh behavior to keep the new
commands consistent with other appointment operations. Share status
updates between the commands to prevent their validation from diverging.
Keep completion independent of scheduled time so recording a completed
visit does not alter its schedule.

Add assertions, validation exceptions and diagnostic logging. Extend
tests for parsing, status transitions, persistence, hidden patients,
unchanged data on rejection, edit preservation and live UI updates.
Update both guides, manual testing instructions and activity diagrams,
including rendered images.

Validation: all 794 tests pass. Java 25 check and coverage tasks,
Checkstyle and repository checks pass.

Appointment commands accept --appt for creation and selection by
timestamp, alongside appointment numbers. The Developer Guide also
conflicts with master's documentation for stricter date rules.

Selecting by timestamp is ambiguous when several visits share the
same date and time. Keeping multiple selection formats also makes
the command interface harder to maintain.

Remove --appt from every command. Make addappt accept a positional
date and optional time, and require appointment numbers for editappt
and deleteappt. Resolve the documentation conflict while preserving
the merged date rules and the branch's appointment behavior.

Appointment numbers identify simultaneous visits reliably, while
one supported format per operation keeps the interface consistent.

Update command help, guides, manual test cases and three diagram
images. Add assertions and focused logging, and extend unit and flow
tests to cover the new formats, rejected legacy flags and persistence.

Verify that all 803 tests and both Checkstyle checks pass.#	docs/DeveloperGuide.md

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix UC08 and UC09 extension numbering
commitResults.messageBody:
The UC08 and UC09 extensions in docs/DeveloperGuide.md appear out of
order and have gaps in their step labels.

This makes the use cases harder to follow and obscures the order of
validation, lookup and clash handling.

Reorder and renumber the extension blocks and their nested response
labels. Place input validation before patient and appointment lookup,
followed by clash warnings.

This order reflects the code: parsing precedes lookup, while clashes
produce warnings after the appointment is added or edited.

Preserve all wording, MSS steps and resume targets. Limit changes to
the UC08 and UC09 extension sections.
